name: Aurorae Sinus
description: Aurorae Sinus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Bay of the Dawn." The name comes from the myth that Aurora held back the dawn. Modern names such as Aurorae Planum and Aurorae Chaos come from it. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.
origin: "Bay of Rosy Dawn"; Aurora held back the dawn.

name: Deltoton Sinus
description: Deltoton Sinus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Bay of the triangle." It earned the name because it forms a triangle with two other classical features, Iapygia and Oenotria. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.
origin: "Bay of the triangle"; makes triangle with Iapygia and Oenotria.

name: Phlegra
description: Phlegra is a classical albedo feature, a patch of the Martian surface mapped from Earth by telescope. Its name means "burning plain" and comes from the Chalcidian Peninsula of Greece, where Zeus was said to have hurled thunderbolts at the Titans to support Hercules. Spacecraft imagery later showed that the area is a belt of eroded mountains and knobby terrain, now called Phlegra Montes, which stretches for nearly 1,400 km (870 mi) between Utopia Planitia and Amazonis Planitia. The mountains were named after the old albedo feature in the 1970s and were first mapped with NASA's Viking images.
origin: "Burning plain;" in Chalcidian Peninsula of Greece where Zeus hurled thunderbolts at Titans to support Hercules.

name: Mare Chronium
description: Mare Chronium is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Cronian Sea." It refers to the northern part of the World Sea of ancient geography, where an eternal dead calm was said to prevail and endanger ships. Planum Chronium and Chronius Mons take their names from it. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.
origin: "Cronian Sea", northern part of World Sea where eternal dead calm, dangerous to ships, prevailed.

name: Trivium Charontis
description: Trivium Charontis is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Crossroad of Charon." It was named as a meeting place of several netherworld canals, the dark lines early observers believed they saw on Mars. It is a wedge-shaped feature near Elysium. Observers reported that it lightened in the 1980s and 1990s, one of several changes seen near Elysium.
origin: "Crossroad of Charon"; meeting place of several netherworld Canals.

name: Deucalionis Regio
description: Deucalionis Regio is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Deucalion's region." In Greek myth, Deucalion was a king of Thessaly who saved himself from a great flood. Light areas on the old maps were mostly named after islands and legendary lands.
origin: "Deucalion's region;" Deucalion was King of Thessaly who saved himself from flood.

name: Chrysokeras
description: Chrysokeras is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Golden Horn." It refers to the inlet of the old Byzantine peninsula, in what is now Turkey.
origin: "Golden Horn"; Byzantine Peninsula (now Turkey), or its inlet.

name: Xanthe
description: Xanthe is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Golden-Yellow Land." Today the name is used for Xanthe Terra, a large highland region just north of the Martian equator. Valleys such as Nanedi Valles and Ravi Vallis cut through it. Scientists have suggested that some landforms there show evidence of precipitation on early Mars, which makes the region useful for studying the planet's wetter past.

name: Dioscuria
description: Dioscuria is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Home of the Dioscuri," the twins Polydeuces and Pollux. It was a symbolic name for the Greek city of Sparta.
origin: "Home of Dioscuri," Polydeuces and Pollux; symbolic name for Sparta.

name: Nilokeras
description: Nilokeras is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Horn of the Nile." On old telescope maps it was part of the Nilus canal. Today the name is used for Nilokeras Scopulus, a long cliff in the northern hemisphere of Mars, about 765 km (475 mi) long and 1 to a little over 2 km (3,300 to 6,600 ft) high. It lies along the southeastern edge of the Tempe Terra plateau and forms the northern wall of the downstream part of Kasei Valles, an immense outflow channel system.
origin: "Horn of the Nile;" part of "Nulus" Canal.

name: Ismenius Lacus
description: Ismenius Lacus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Ismenian Lake." Ismenia is a poetic term for the Greek city of Thebes. The name now also labels the Ismenius Lacus quadrangle (MC-5), one of 30 map sheets of Mars made by the U.S. Geological Survey, which covers part of the northern lowlands between 30 and 65 degrees north latitude. Scientists find two places in it especially interesting: Deuteronilus Mensae and Protonilus Mensae.
origin: "Ismenian Lake"; Ismenia is poetic term for Thebes.

name: Niliacus Lacus
description: Niliacus Lacus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Lake of the Nile." The modern name Colles Nili, for a group of hills, comes from it. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.

name: Phoenicis Lacus
description: Phoenicis Lacus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Lake of the Phoenix," a reference to Arabia or India. The name now also labels the Phoenicis Lacus quadrangle (MC-17), one of 30 map sheets of Mars made by the U.S. Geological Survey. It covers part of the Tharsis rise, a huge uplift built from lava flows. The volcanoes Pavonis Mons and Arsia Mons are believed to have once had glaciers on them.
origin: "Lake of the Phoenix;" Arabia or India.

name: Solis Lacus
description: Solis Lacus is a dark patch on Mars whose Latin name means "lake of the sun." It was once called "Oculus" and is still widely known as the Eye of Mars, because with the lighter area around it, called Thaumasia, it looks like the pupil of an eye. It sits south of Valles Marineris. Solis Lacus is famous for changing its size and shape over the years. Astronomers once puzzled over this, but spacecraft images later showed that wind-blown dust is responsible, especially during dust storms. Around the turn of the 20th century, Percival Lowell believed it was the capital of Mars, because so many of the canals he claimed to see seemed to meet there. Those canals were later shown not to exist.
origin: "Lake of the Sun"; the so-called "Eye of Mars," connecting East with West.

name: Uchronia
description: Uchronia is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Land of Agelessness," or roughly "nowhen."

name: Thymiamata
description: Thymiamata is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Land of sweet-scented perfumes." It refers to South Yemen or India, lands known for incense.
origin: "Land of sweet-scented perfumes"; South Yemen or India.

name: Eunostos
description: Eunostos is a classical albedo feature whose name means "lucky journey or lucky return." It refers to the infernal regions beyond Elysium.
origin: "Lucky journey or lucky return"; i.e., infernal regions beyond Elysium.

name: Sinus Meridiani
description: Sinus Meridiani is a dark albedo feature stretching east to west just south of the Martian equator. Its name means "Meridian Bay" or "Middle Bay," and it was named by the French astronomer Camille Flammarion in the late 1870s. Many people now know the region as Meridiani Planum, because NASA's Mars Exploration Rover Opportunity landed there in 2004. For a time between 1979 and 2001 the nearby area was called Terra Meridiani.

name: Moeris Lacus
description: Moeris Lacus is a classical albedo feature named for Lake Moeris, an Egyptian lake in the Fayum region of the Libyan Desert. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.
origin: "Moeris Lake;" Moeris was Egyptian lake in Libyan Desert.

name: Mare Boreum
description: Mare Boreum means "North Sea." It is the older name for the feature now called Planum Boreum, the large plain around the north polar ice cap. The name is now used for the Mare Boreum quadrangle (MC-1), a U.S. Geological Survey map sheet covering everything north of 65 degrees latitude, including the polar cap, which is roughly 1,100 km (680 mi) across. NASA's Phoenix lander touched down on Vastitas Borealis in this region on May 25, 2008.

name: Phaethontis
description: Phaethontis is a classical albedo feature named for Phaethon, the Greek mythological character who recklessly drove the chariot of the Sun. The name is now used for the Phaethontis quadrangle in the southern hemisphere of Mars. That region contains the large crater Hipparchus, the crater Ptolemaeus, the chaos regions Gorgonum Chaos and Atlantis Chaos, and a set of small channels called Tader Valles.
origin: "Of Phaethon;" who recklessly drove Chariot of Sun.

name: Margaritifer Sinus
description: Margaritifer Sinus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Pearl Bay," after the Pearl Coast of southern India. The name is now used for the Margaritifer Sinus quadrangle (MC-19), a region just south of the equator that includes channel systems such as Parana Valles and Samara Valles. The rim of Endeavour Crater, which NASA's rover Opportunity explored, also lies within this quadrangle.
origin: "Pearl Bay," after Pearl Coast, South India.

name: Phrixi Regio
description: Phrixi Regio is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Phrixus' Region." In Greek myth, Phrixus and his sister Helle escaped being sacrificed in Boeotia by riding away on a ram. The cliff Phrixi Rupes takes its name from it. Light areas on the old maps were mostly named after islands and legendary lands.
origin: "Phrixus' Region;" Phrixus and sister Helle escaped sacrifice in Boeotia on back of ram with golden fleece.

name: Protei Regio
description: Protei Regio is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Proteus' Region." Proteus was a sea god with the gift of prophecy. Light areas on the old maps were mostly named after islands and legendary lands.
origin: "Proteus' Region;" Proteus was a sea god with a gift of prophecy.

name: Pyrrhae Regio
description: Pyrrhae Regio is a classical albedo feature named for Pyrrha, the wife of Deucalion, who survived the great flood in Greek myth. Pyrrhae Chaos and Pyrrhae Fossae take their names from it. Light areas on the old maps were mostly named after islands and legendary lands.
origin: "Pyrrha's Region;" named for Pyrrha, wife of Deucalion.

name: Ogygis Regio
description: Ogygis Regio is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Region of Ogygos." Ogygos was an ancient king of Thebes or Athens in Greece. The name is also used for Ogygis Undae, the only named dune field in the southern hemisphere of Mars. Its dunes cover an area of about 1,904 square km. Because the field is so large, it is a major subject of research into the shape of Martian dunes and the composition of their sand.
origin: "Region of Ogygos;" Ogygos was ancient King of Thebes or Athens, Greece.

name: Mare Sirenum
description: Mare Sirenum is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Sea of the Sirens." Terra Sirenum is named after it. Amateur and professional observers have recorded changes here, including a weakening that may have come from dust settling after earlier storms. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.

name: Argyre
description: Argyre takes its name from a map made by Giovanni Schiaparelli in 1877. It refers to Argyre, a mythical island of silver at the mouth of the Ganges River. Spacecraft later showed that the bright area is Argyre Planitia, a plain on the floor of a huge impact basin in the southern highlands. The basin is about 1,700 km (1,100 mi) wide and drops 5.2 km (17,000 ft) below the surrounding plains. It is the second deepest impact basin on Mars after Hellas. It formed when an object about 200 km (120 mi) wide struck Mars between 4 and 3.8 billion years ago, during the Late Heavy Bombardment. It may be one of the best preserved ancient impact basins from that time. On its east rim, Galle Crater looks like a smiley face.
origin: "Silver" Island at mouth of Ganges River; present-day Arakan, Burma.

name: Nix Olympica
description: Nix Olympica means "Snows of Olympus." Giovanni Schiaparelli gave it this name in 1879 because early telescopic observers could only see differences in brightness on Mars, not height. It looked like a bright patch, perhaps a snow-covered mountain. In 1969 Mariners 6 and 7 photographed a curious ring-shaped feature there, and radar showed it was one of the highest points on Mars. In November 1971, NASA's Mariner 9 arrived at Mars during a planet-wide dust storm, and the summit of this feature poked above the dust. Mariner 9 images showed that the bright patch is a giant shield volcano. The name Olympus Mons was then adopted for the volcano, to tell it apart from the albedo feature. Olympus Mons is about 600 km across and is the tallest volcano in the Solar System.
origin: "Snows of Olympus;" Olympus was mountain home of gods in Greece.

name: Mare Australe
description: Mare Australe means "South Sea." It is the older name for the feature now called Planum Australe, the large plain around the south polar ice cap. The name is now used for the Mare Australe quadrangle (MC-30), a U.S. Geological Survey map sheet covering all of Mars south of 65 degrees latitude, including the south polar cap. NASA's Mars Polar Lander was lost in this region during its 1999 landing attempt.

name: Nereidum Fretum
description: Nereidum Fretum is a classical albedo feature whose name means "Straits of the Nereids," the sea nymphs of Greek myth. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.
origin: "Straits of the Nereids", who were sea nymphs.

name: Hesperia
description: Hesperia is a classical albedo feature. Its name is an old Greek name for Italy, or for Spain in Roman times. Today it is best known as Hesperia Planum, a broad lava plain in the southern highlands. The Hesperian period of Martian history is named after it. This was a time of widespread volcanic activity and catastrophic floods that carved huge outflow channels. During the Hesperian, Mars changed from the wetter and perhaps warmer world of the Noachian to the dry, cold, dusty planet seen today. Scientists are unsure when it ended, with estimates ranging from 3,200 to 2,000 million years ago and 3,000 million years ago often cited.
origin: "The Occiden"; name for Italy (Greek); or Spain (Roman) or West area of Ethiopians where sun sank.

name: Ceraunius
description: Ceraunius means "Thunderclap" and is named for the Ceraunii Mountains on the coast of Epirus, Greece. The name is used for Ceraunius Fossae, a set of fractures in the northern Tharsis region of Mars. The trenches there are commonly several kilometers wide and between 100 and just over 1,000 m deep, packed closely together to give the land a rugged pattern of ridges and grooves. The nearby volcano Ceraunius Tholus carries the name too.
origin: "Thunderclap"; named for Ceraunii Mountains on coast of Epirus, Greece.

name: Tithonius Lacus
description: Tithonius Lacus is a classical albedo feature named for Tithonus, who received eternal life but not eternal youth from his wife Eos. Tithonium Chasma, a canyon of Valles Marineris, takes its name from it. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.
origin: "Tithonian Lake"; Tithonus received from his wife Eos eternal life but not eternal youth.

name: Tractus Albus
description: Tractus Albus is a classical albedo feature whose name means "White Tract" in Latin.

name: Alitus
description: Alitus is a small impact crater on Mars, about 50 km across. Its name comes from the town of Alytus in Lithuania. Martian craters are often named after towns and villages on Earth with populations under 100,000. An impact crater is a bowl-shaped hole left when a space rock strikes a planet's surface.

name: Belyov
description: Belyov is a small impact crater on Mars, about 0.2 km across. Its name comes from the town of Belev in the Tula region of Russia. Martian craters are often named after towns and villages on Earth with populations under 100,000. An impact crater is a bowl-shaped hole left when a space rock strikes a planet's surface.

name: Tyuratam
description: Tyuratam is a small impact crater on Mars, about 0.3 km across. Its name comes from Tyuratam (Toretam), a township in Kazakhstan. Martian craters are often named after towns and villages on Earth with populations under 100,000. An impact crater is a bowl-shaped hole left when a space rock strikes a planet's surface.

name: Voeykov
description: Voeykov is an impact crater on Mars, about 75 km across. It is named after A. I. Voeykov, a Russian climatologist and geographer (1842 to 1916). Many Martian craters honor scientists who contributed to the study of Mars, as well as writers and others who added to its lore. An impact crater is a bowl-shaped hole left when a space rock strikes a planet's surface.
origin: A. I.; Russian climatologist and geographer (1842-1916).

name: Arkhangelsky
description: Arkhangelsky is an impact crater on Mars, about 117 km across. It is named after A.D. Arkhangelsky, a Russian geologist. Many Martian craters honor scientists who contributed to the study of Mars, as well as writers and others who added to its lore. An impact crater is a bowl-shaped hole left when a space rock strikes a planet's surface.

name: Mare Hadriacum
description: Mare Hadriacum is a classical albedo feature named for the Adriatic Sea. The volcanic features Hadriacus Mons and Hadriaca Patera take their names from it. Early observers such as Schiaparelli thought dark patches like this were seas or lakes. We now know they are areas where wind has swept away pale dust, exposing a darker, often basaltic surface.

name: Krishtofovich
description: Krishtofovich is an impact crater about 112 km across, named after Afrikan Nikolayevich Krishtofovich (1885 to 1953), a Soviet geologist, paleobotanist, and botanist. He was a fossil hunter who specialized in plants from the Mesozoic era, the age of the dinosaurs. In 1932 he published a book called Geological Review of the Countries of the Far East. His crater name was approved in 1982.

name: Caralis Chaos
description: Caralis Chaos is an area of chaos terrain, a part of the surface where ridges, cracks, and plains look jumbled and tangled together. It is about 103.35 km across. The International Astronomical Union approved the name in 2014. Like most chaos areas, it is named after a classical albedo feature, one of the light and dark patches that astronomers such as Schiaparelli mapped from Earth before the space age.
origin: After Caralis Fons, classical albedo feature named after Caralis Lacus, now Beysehir Gölü, in Isauria (Asia Minor).

name: Apollinaris Sulci
description: Apollinaris Sulci is a group of sets of roughly parallel furrows and ridges (sulci) on Mars, spanning about 189 km. It takes its name from a classical albedo feature near 5°S, 187°W, a light or dark patch seen from Earth by telescope.

It was named after the nearby classical albedo feature Ausonia, a name that refers to a country of the Aruncii, called Ausones in Greek.

name: Galaxias Fluctūs
description: Galaxias Fluctūs is an area of flow terrain (fluctus) on Mars, spanning about 607 km. It takes its name from a nearby classical albedo feature, a light or dark patch seen from Earth by telescope.

name: Galaxias Fossae
description: Galaxias Fossae is a group of troughs in the Cebrenia quadrangle of Mars, more than 500 km long. The word "fossae" is used for large troughs on Mars, and the name comes from the classical albedo feature Galaxias. Troughs like these, also called grabens, form when the crust is stretched until it breaks. Two cracks form and the middle section drops down, leaving steep cliffs along the sides. Sometimes a line of pits forms as material collapses into a void created by the stretching. Galaxias Fossae is one of several trough systems on Mars, along with Cerberus Fossae, Elysium Fossae, and Hephaestus Fossae.

name: Syrtis Major Planum
description: Syrtis Major Planum, is a massive shield volcano in the eastern hemisphere of Mars . Discovered in 1659 , It was the first surface feature ever recognized on another planet and was used to calculate the length of a Martian day .  It is situated  in the Syrtis Major quadrangle ¸, The floors of the calderas are unique among large Martian volcanoes as they are not elevated relative to the terrain surrounding Syrtis Major . This place is very rich in Silica-rich and ultramafic olivine-rich lavas materials which are found within Nili Patera and cover part of Syrtis Major Planum's slopes .This would be very crucial on future missions. Syrtis Major Planum's rich and complex volcanic history make it unique on Mars .
origin: Albedo feature name; changed from Planitia to Planum.

name: Amazonis Sulci
description: Amazonis Sulci is a group of sets of roughly parallel furrows and ridges (sulci) on Mars, spanning about 251 km. It takes its name from the albedo feature Amazonis, the home of the Amazons.

name: Arsia Mons
description: Arsia Mons is a massive shield-looking volcano located around the equator of mars. Its unique, gentle slopes looks like a warriors shield, (hence the name shield-volcano). Various ice glaciers have formed around the flanks of this volcano making this spot another hot-spot for finding ancient bio-signatures. Moreover, the presence of both water and lava tubes makes it one of the few ideal locations for cost-effective temporary human bases on mars. Arsia Mons also generates massive seasonal water-ice clouds during the southern autumn and winter. Scientists and researchers can study these clouds to learn about cloud formation, atmospheric circulation and local Martian weather patterns.

name: Ascraeus Mons
description: Ascraeus Mons is an extinct (possibly inactive) shield-shaped volcano which is located close to the equator of mars. Together with Pavonis and Arsia Mons, it forms a striking volcanic alignment across Mars. This volcano contains pits which lead into deep lava tubes (tubes made of settled lava or basalt) with huge deposits of fan-shaped ice glaciers right beside them! This means that under the right circumstances, this region could become a temporary cost-effective base for humans on mars. This volcano was last active around 100 million years ago, so it became inactive quite recently. This means by studying the lava flow and geological structure of the volcano, scientists can study about how volcanic activity shaped the Martian crust.

name: Aeolis Mons
description: Aeolis Mons is a massive central mountain peak inside Gale Crater on the planet Mars. It has exposed layers which record changes in Mars geological and environmental conditions over time. NASA’s Curiosity rover has been studying these rocks since 2012 to help us understand the atmosphere, environment and geological history of mars. The many layers of this mountain clearly displays the geological history of planet mars in incredible detail. Researching these layers proves many theories such as the existence of water and other minerals on mars. This mountain is a treasure-trove for astronauts looking to unveil the mysteries of mars history and its many wonders!

name: Aeolis Palus
description: Aeolis Palus is a plain about 112 km (70 mi) across on the northern floor of Gale Crater, between the crater wall and the foothills of Aeolis Mons, also called Mount Sharp. It became famous on August 6, 2012, when NASA's Curiosity rover landed there. The International Astronomical Union approved the name on May 16, 2012, a few months before touchdown. It comes from Aeolis, a classical albedo feature (a light or dark patch mapped from Earth by telescope) that was adopted in 1958 and recalls a floating island in Greek myth where the winds were kept in a cave. On August 22, 2012, NASA named Curiosity's exact landing spot Bradbury Landing, in honor of author Ray Bradbury, whose stories, including The Martian Chronicles, inspired many people to dream of Mars. From here, Curiosity set out toward the base of Aeolis Mons to study its layered rocks.

description: The Alba Mons is the largest volcano on mars in terms of surface area (upto 3000 km or about the width of the US). The northern region around the volcano shows signs of substantial amounts of sub-surface water which is essential for human-led martian missions. Lava tubes (Tubes formed from cooled down lava) are also available just under the volcano which can serve as cost-effective and relatively safe temporary bases for humans on mars. Moreover, studying the volcano’s unique characteristics like its flat structure and rather absurd lava-flow patterns could answer new questions related to martian terrain and history, which makes it a very important site for future astronauts to dig into.

description: Argyre Planitia is a large basin formed by a colossal asteroid impact around 3.9 billion years ago. Its known that this basin filled with water following the impact which formed a lake roughly the size of the Mediterranean Sea. It has also been found that there was liquid water below layers of ice in this basin. Due to its history as a large water body, the Argyre Planitia Impact basin has abundant surface water in the form of ice and is very deep. name: Elysium Mons
description: The Elysium Mons is considered to the youngest volcano on mars. The last time it was active was only 2.5 million year to 53,000 years ago (which is basically yesterday in geological terms!). meaning there is much that can be extracted by studying the surrounding area as well as the lava flow in this region. its relatively recent lava flows offer an unprecedented window into Mars’ thermal evolution, while volcanic heat interactions with subsurface ice create prime environments for investigating past microbial life. For astronauts having sub-surface ice close to their landing area is huge, moreover this region also has a relatively low elevation which means it is a prime location for space crafts to land and for astronauts to build bases!

name: Elysium Planitia
description: Elysium Mons is a very large volcano on Mars located in the planet's eastern hemisphere. Its structure differs from the giant Tharsis volcanoes, with relatively few obvious lava flows on its flanks. Studying these differences can help scientists understand how volcanic activity varied across different regions of Mars. About 6.5 km north west to this volcano is a martian crater formed by nakhlites-a specific class of basaltic Martian meteorites recovered on Earth. Sampling rock formations directly at their source allows scientists to calibrate the exact cosmic and geological timeline of Mars' interior evolution. Sub-surface ice is present very close to the volcano and it is possible that due to the interaction between molten volcanic magma and subsurface ice a prime, sheltered environment for microbial life may have existed at one time in the past.

name: Hebes Chasma
description: Hebes Chasma is a deep canyon about 317 km (197 mi) long, just north of Valles Marineris. Unlike most canyons nearby, it is a closed basin with no channel leading out of it. A large mound of layered material, Hebes Mensa, rises from its floor. Mars Express and other orbiters detected sulfate minerals in these layers, which scientists link to water in Mars's past. The canyon is named after the nearby classical albedo feature Hebes, named for the goddess of youth.

name: Hellas Planitia
description: Hellas Planitia  is a plain located within the huge, roughly circular impact basic Hellas located in the southern hemisphere of mars. This plain is about 7.1 km deep into mars and has the highest atmospheric pressure and has the best atmospheric shielding from the harsh environment of mars. The atmospheric pressure is so high that liquid water can even exist there briefly without evaporating. Moreover, this region has many, many ice glaciers and there are also signs of hydrothermal lake environments (which is ideal for microbial life to thrive). Overall, this regions has arguably one of the best, if not the best odds for a space mission to be successfully carried out due to both its relatively habitable location and the probable existence of ancient microbial fossils.

description: Iani Chaos is an area of chaos terrain, where the ground has broken into jumbled blocks and tangled plains. It is about 450 km (280 mi) across. The International Astronomical Union approved the name in 1976, after the classical albedo feature Iani. It sits at the head of Ares Vallis, a huge outflow channel that runs north to Chryse Planitia. Chaos terrain like this is thought to form when ice or water trapped underground is released, letting the surface collapse and sending floods downstream. NASA's Mars Pathfinder landed in the Ares Vallis flood plain in 1997.

name: Isidis Planitia
description: Isidis Planitia is a plain located within a giant impact basin on mars, located partly in the Syrtis Major quadrangle and partly in the Amenthes quadrangle. Data from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter detected extensive deposits of magnesium carbonate around the basin rim, which means that there is a good possibility of ancient microbial life to have existed here at one time. This is because Carbonates require liquid water that is non-acidic (pH-neutral) to form—creating environmental conditions far more hospitable for the evolution and preservation of ancient microbial life. Moreover, being the 3rd largest impact basin on mars, its low elevation provides a thicker atmospheric shield overhead making landing and setting up base much easier here than many other locations.

Orbiters have found sulfate minerals in these layers, which usually form in the presence of water, so scientists study the canyon for clues to Mars's wetter past. Water is thought to have burst out of this region long ago and flowed north through Maja Valles.

Olympus Mons on Mars is a prime scientific target for future human exploration because it holds accessible water frost, offers potential shelter within deep volcanic structures, and provides a window into the planet's volcanic history.

name: Utopia Planitia
description: The famous Utopia Planitia from  the Star Trek franchise  is actually one of three major basins in Mars’ northern hemisphere, the largest recongnized impact basin on the mars and on the solar system. It has a size just under twice the north-south size of Earth’s Sahara Desert.  The Utopia basin is estimated to have formed around 4.3-4.1 billion years ago. NASA reported finding a large amount of underground ice in the Utopia Planitia region.Utopia, holding major importance for understanding the planet's geological and climatic history. There has been major signs of large amount of underground ice in this region making it a very important site or future missions . Other than that , Utopia holds  major importance for understanding the planet's geological and climatic history.

name: Vastitas Borealis
description: Vastitas Borealis, is the largest unconfirmed impact basin on Mars, and also the largest low-lying plain on Mars. The planitia formed around 4 billion years ago when a Pluto-sized object collided with the early Mars. It resides near the north pole, surrounding Planum Boreum, and also has several other features and ridges on the plain, such as rupes groups and major colles formations. This is also one of the oldest regions, and its formation may have shaped Mars' geology to what it is today.

Like most chaos areas, it is named after a classical albedo feature, one of the light and dark patches that astronomers such as Schiaparelli mapped from Earth before the space age.

name: Planum Australe
description: Planum Australe is the southern polar plain on Mars . The circular plain spans roughly 1,430 kilometers across. The geology of this region was to be explored by the failed NASA mission Mars Polar Lander, which lost contact on entry into the Martian atmosphere . Planum Australe is partially covered by a permanent polar ice cap composed of frozen water and carbon dioxide about 3 km thick. It is possible that the area of this ice cap may be shrinking due to localized climate change . September 2020, scientists confirmed the existence of several large saltwater lakes under the ice in the south polar region of the planet Mars , which just like the north pole is a very important information for the next human’s landing on mars.

description: Alba Patera is the central caldera complex of Alba Mons, a huge and very low volcano in northern Tharsis. The name comes from the classical albedo feature Alba. The caldera complex is about 66 km (41 mi) across, but it is only a small part of the volcano. Gentle lava flows spread out for more than 1,000 km (620 mi), which makes Alba the largest volcano on Mars by area, even though it stands far lower than neighbors such as Olympus Mons. Its flanks are cut by ridges, channels and fractures.

His long series of Mars observations passed to Johannes Kepler, who used them to work out the laws of planetary motion.

name: Holden
description: The holden crater is considered to be one of the most well-preserved lakes on mars. The crater features very shallow and clear clay layers which have a high chance of hosting possible microbial life. Multiple floods occurred in this area over time, especially when water flowed in from the Uzboi Vallis water body. What this means is that the geological diversity which is present here will give researchers a very good sample to learn about Mar’s history and geological profile, moreover being a crater, having low elevation and having such high-quality research samples proves that this region is a prime pick for the purpose of research and human settlement. Because of its potential habitability and safety profile, Holden crater survived repeated selection cuts and was named a top finalist for both NASA's Curiosity rover and Perseverance rover  missions before Gale Crater and Jezero Crater were ultimately chosen.

name: Syrtis Major
description: Syrtis Major is the most conspicuous dark marking on Mars as seen from Earth. Giovanni Schiaparelli named it in 1877 after the Roman name for the body of water off the coast of Libya known today as the Gulf of Sidra. It is a dusky, wedge-shaped region that reaches about 1,500 km (930 mi) north from the equator and spans about 1,000 km from west to east. It was the first permanent feature recorded on the surface of another planet, in sketches made by the Dutch astronomer Christiaan Huygens in 1659. By watching it cross the face of Mars, Huygens worked out that a Martian day is slightly longer than an Earth day. Its outline has changed noticeably over the years.

name: Mariner
description: Mariner is a crater about 155 km (96 mi) across in the southern highlands. It is named for the Mariner 4 spacecraft, which flew past Mars on July 14, 1965. Mariner 4 sent back 22 pictures covering about 1 percent of the planet, the first close-up images of another planet beamed to Earth. The 11th image was dominated by this crater, and the pictures stunned scientists by showing a heavily cratered surface that looked more like the Moon than the Mars of earlier imagination. The International Astronomical Union named the crater Mariner in 1967 to honor the discovery. A ridge belonging to Sirenum Fossae crosses the crater in the original image. In March 1999, NASA's Mars Global Surveyor photographed a small part of the crater floor at 1.5 m (5 ft) per pixel, giving a modern view of the place where Mars first looked cratered.

name: Athabasca Valles
description: Athabasca Valles is a system of channels about 270 to 285 km (170 to 177 mi) long in Elysium Planitia, roughly 1,000 km (620 mi) southeast of the volcano Elysium Mons. The name was approved in 1997 and honors the Athabasca River in Canada. It was changed from Athabasca Vallis when it was recognized as a network of channels. Viking Orbiter images first showed it as an outflow channel, a valley carved by a huge, sudden release of fluid. It starts at the Cerberus Fossae, a set of long cracks in the ground. Athabasca is thought to be the youngest outflow channel on Mars, only about 2 to 20 million years old, which is very recent in geologic terms. Scientists still debate what carved it. Features such as streamlined islands suggest flooding by water, but high resolution images from the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter showed the channels are draped by a thin layer of solidified lava. Many researchers think both water and lava played a part.
origin: River in Canada. (Changed from Athabasca Vallis.)

Since its believed that the water here was not stagnant, but rather flowing (due to abundant iron/magnesium smectite clays throughout the delta). name: Gale
description: : Gale is a crater, and a probable dry lake, in the northwestern part of mars. Evidence gathered by NASA's Curiosity rover confirms that, in the past Gale Crater hosted a long-lived system of ancient freshwater lakes and streams. The mudstone deposits show that water persisted here for millions of years with a near-neutral pH, providing all the key ingredients (carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, sulfur, and phosphorus) necessary for life to thrive. Moreover, Tests conducted inside Gale Crater have detected a wide array of organic compounds like benzene and other complex carbon chains trapped within the mudstone layers. These characteristics make this one of the most ideal places on mars to look for pre-existing microbial life and for researching ancient prebiotic chemistry.

name: Nirgal Vallis
description: Nirgal Vallis is a long, winding valley south of Valles Marineris, roughly 500 to 600 km (310 to 370 mi) long. Nirgal is the Babylonian word for Mars. Unlike the big outflow channels, it has short, stubby tributaries and steep, rounded ends. That shape is often linked to groundwater slowly seeping out of the ground and eroding the rock, a process called sapping. It is one of the best examples on Mars of a valley that may have formed from groundwater rather than rainfall or giant floods.

name: Ares Vallis
description: Ares Vallis is a massive outflow channel formed by catastrophic ancient floods that rushed across Mars billions of years ago. This has created a relatively flat-area for martian missions to be accomplished. Moreover, due to the flood various types of rocks from thousands of kilometers have been washed up in this channel, that is, it is a very convenient location for astronauts to conduct research and collect information. Research shows that interconnected lakes existed along the equatorial region near Ares Vallis, this information proves the existence of vast water-ways in mars billions of years ago. This means that there is a relatively high chance of biosignatures or past life in this region, thus it is an essential and high-priority region for human-led expeditions to mars. NASA’s Pathfinder mission also landed here in 1997, allowing scientists to examine rocks and soil transported by these ancient processes.
